perf.summary: Brute-force O(n^2 · matchLen) longest-previous-factor search; replace with a suffix-automaton / suffix-array LPF or hash-chain to reach near-linear LZ factorization.
perf.currentCost: For each i it scans all j<i (line 24) and extends byte-by-byte (line 27), giving O(n^2 · avgMatchLen) — the classic quadratic LZ factorization. Dominant cost.
perf.proposedChange: Compute the LZ factorization via a suffix automaton or the LPF array from a suffix array + LCP (Crochemore/Ilie), or a bounded hash-chain match finder, all expressible with native stackalloc arrays.
perf.rationale: Drops the asymptotic from quadratic to O(n) or O(n log n), the single largest improvement for this routine on non-trivial inputs.
perf.risk: The current code selects the longest match and ties break to the smallest j (first found, strict `>`). An LPF/automaton must reproduce the same length and the same chosen position to keep output bit-identical; if only length-equivalence is required (any valid factor of max length), the constraint relaxes. State which contract holds before swapping.

perf.summary: Hoist invariant bound and remove redundant per-byte comparison in the inner extend loop; remove misleading AggressiveInlining on this large method.
perf.currentCost: Inner loop tests `i + l < len && j + l < i` each byte; `len` and the `j < i` cap are loop-invariant-derivable into a single `maxL = min(len - i, i - j)` bound, halving the per-byte comparisons. Also `[MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)]` on this large method only bloats I-cache.
perf.proposedChange: Precompute `int maxL = (len - i) < (i - j) ? (len - i) : (i - j); int l = 0; while (l < maxL && input[j+l] == input[i+l]) l++;` and drop the AggressiveInlining attribute.
perf.rationale: One bound compare per byte instead of two, with the bound branchless-min'd once per j; fewer instructions on the hottest loop. Attribute removal avoids needless code-size growth.
perf.risk: min(len-i, i-j) exactly reproduces the original two-condition termination, so output unchanged. AggressiveInlining removal is a hint-only change.
